title: BATS oxygen loss on sigma-theta 26.5 persists after same-cruise deep-water subtraction, 1989-2025
abstract: Question: can a common oxygen offset explain BATS oxygen loss and the early swings missed by a decadal outcrop model? We form oxygen differences within each cruise from BATS bottle data v10. From 1989-1998 to 2016-2025, oxygen on sigma-theta 26.5 fell by 11.18 umol/kg. Oxygen at 2000 and 3000 m fell by about 1.0. The upper-minus-deep differences fell by 10.05 and 10.07 umol/kg; two-year block bootstrap intervals are -11.98 to -8.16 and -12.30 to -7.89. The deep-to-deep difference changed by -0.02 (-1.25 to +1.32). The upper swings near 1997-2003, 2003-2012 and 2012-2021 retain their signs with both references. Results hold with a 200 m interpolation bracket, after excluding 1989-1991 from the reference, and in winter and summer. A ratio that cancels both gains and offsets proved unstable because the deep oxygen difference was small. Nutrient changes replicate prior evidence for regenerated material; early nitrate changes are uncertain. A uniform additive oxygen offset cannot remove the upper loss. Deep-specific measurement errors, real deep changes, gain errors and interpolation errors remain possible. The test does not identify the missing ocean process or validate the outcrop mechanism quantitatively.
